text: Welcome to this made-up tutorial about planning a small vegetable garden.
Today we cover three things: picking a spot, preparing the soil and choosing plants.
First, the spot. Most vegetables want six or more hours of direct sun.
Walk around your yard in the morning and again in the afternoon.
Write down where the shade falls at each time.
Next, water. Pick a spot close to a hose or a rain barrel.
Carrying water across the yard gets old fast.
Now the soil. Dig a small hole and squeeze a handful of soil.
If it crumbles, that is a good sign.
If it sticks together like clay, mix in compost before planting.
A raised bed is another option when the ground is hard.
Fill it with a mix of topsoil and compost.
Then the plants. Start with a few that forgive mistakes.
Lettuce, bush beans and zucchini are common first choices.
Read the seed packet for spacing and planting dates.
Crowded plants compete for light and water.
Keep a simple notebook: what you planted, where and when.
Next season the notebook tells you what to change.
Water deeply once or twice a week instead of a little every day.
Deep watering helps roots grow down.
Pull weeds while they are small.
A layer of mulch keeps weeds down and the soil moist.
Check the leaves every few days for holes or spots.
Pick off damaged leaves early.
Harvest lettuce leaves from the outside in.
Pick beans while they are thin and tender.
Zucchini grows fast, so check it every day in summer.
That is the whole plan: sun, water, soil, a few easy plants and a notebook.
Thanks for watching this made-up example.
